title: Redis Data Structures & Persistence
definition: In-memory key-value data store providing sub-millisecond operations, automatic RAM eviction, and dual persistence engines.

keyPoints.title: In-Memory Structures
keyPoints.description: Strings, Hashes, Lists, Sets & ZSets held in volatile RAM for sub-millisecond access.

keyPoints.title: TTL & Eviction
keyPoints.description: Key expiration and memory policies (noeviction, allkeys-lru, volatile-lru) when RAM fills up.

keyPoints.title: Dual Persistence
keyPoints.description: RDB point-in-time snapshots + AOF continuous append-log for crash durability and recovery.

recap: Redis RAM-based key-value store hai jisme Strings, Hashes, Lists, Sets aur Sorted Sets sub-millisecond operations dete hain. Memory limited hone ki wajah se TTL aur maxmemory eviction policies (noeviction vs allkeys-lru) tay karti hain ki memory bharne par data delete hoga ya write fail. Crash safety ke liye RDB periodic photos aur AOF continuous write-log milkar data recover karte hain.

demos.title: String: one key, one value
demos.summary: Ek key ke andar ek value: counter, JSON cache, ya raw string. Redis ke liye value sirf bytes hai.

demos.title: Hash: fields inside a key
demos.summary: Ek session key ke andar alag fields. Role badlo ya login count badhao — poora object rewrite nahi hota.

demos.title: List vs Set: order or uniqueness
demos.summary: Same search events, do alag guarantees: List order aur duplicates rakhti hai; Set sirf unique values.

demos.title: Sorted set: score decides rank
demos.summary: Har player ka score hi uska rank hai. Score badla, rank khud badal jaata hai — manual sorting nahi.

demos.title: TTL vs eviction: why a key disappears
demos.summary: TTL time se key hatata hai; eviction memory full hone par policy se key chunta hai. Same result, alag reason.

demos.title: RDB vs AOF: what survives a crash
demos.summary: RDB last snapshot tak ka data deta hai; AOF fsynced commands replay karta hai. Crash karke khud difference dekho.
